bib.title: Few-shot Learning with Multilingual Generative Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 11699-11732

read.skipped: Appendix D.3-F tables (full FLORES grid, social-value tables, data card language statistics) skimmed for prose only; numeric grids not transcribed.

question: How well do multilingual generative language models perform zero- and few-shot in-context learning across many languages, and which prompting approaches work for non-English tasks?
hypothesis: A decoder-only model pretrained on a balanced 30-language corpus will match or beat a comparable English-centric GPT-3 on multilingual few-shot tasks, and cross-lingual prompting (English templates, cross-lingual demonstrations) will transfer.
contributions: Four multilingual decoder-only LMs (XGLM 564M, 1.7B, 2.9B, 7.5B) trained on 500B tokens in 30 languages
Comprehensive study of multilingual zero/few-shot learning, including prompting approaches and cross-lingual transfer through templates and demonstrations
New dataset XStoryCloze (professional translation of English StoryCloze into 10 languages)

method.summary: Train GPT-3-style decoder-only causal LMs on CC100-XL (30 languages, upsampled, 250k joint SentencePiece vocabulary) for up to 500B tokens, then evaluate with 0/1/4/32/128-shot in-context learning on multilingual NLU, MT and English tasks against GPT-3 Curie, an in-house English replication and a translate-test baseline.
method.task: multilingual causal language-model pretraining and in-context few-shot evaluation (NLU, MT)

datasets.name: CC100-XL

API (Ada, Babbage, Curie also used for MT)

training.hardware: XGLM 7.5B: 256 A100 GPUs, data parallel, Fairseq
training.compute: about 3 weeks on 256 A100 GPUs at 311.6k words per second (7.5B)

other.vocab_training: unigram LM on 10 million sentences sampled with multinomial alpha=0.3 (Lample and Conneau 2019)

inference.decoding: greedy for machine translation; classification and multiple choice by arg-max of LM scoring function
inference.samples: 5 runs, each with a different random set of few-shot examples; k in {0,1,4,32,128}
inference.prompting: cloze-style template with [Mask] and verbalizer; demonstrations concatenated with [Sep]; examples truncated to 2048 tokens keeping only whole demonstrations; English-centric tasks use Brown et al. prompts with newline separator

parameters.scoring: average of per-token log-probabilities ignoring the common prefix of candidates (selected on held-out XNLI, XCOPA, XStoryCloze dev), no calibration

other.inference_speed: 256 A100 GPUs: 1.47 million words per second; 8 V100 GPUs: 6 hours to evaluate XGLM 7.5B on XStoryCloze

results.claim: Only 32.6% of XGLM's 500B-token data is English (163B tokens, about 54% of GPT-3's English).
XGLM 7.5B was trained on 256 A100 GPUs for about 3 weeks.
Cross-lingual demonstrations and a good (English) template effects do not add up; with a better prompt the demonstration transfer benefit is generally cancelled.
On XNLI, accuracy rises from k=0 to 4 but falls at k=32 and above; PAWS-X stays near random (50%) at all k.

limits: Authors did not ablate the inadvertent over-sampling of ko, fi, th, bg, ca, hi, et due to extreme computational cost.
Non-English evaluation data are (professional) translations, which may inflate cross-lingual transfer (Artetxe et al. 2020); translate-test baseline may also be inflated.

English data is 54% of GPT-3's, and training corpora differ (CommonCrawl only vs. BookCorpus/Wikipedia), so the English gap is confounded with data quality and the curse of multilinguality; no controlled experiment.
Only decoder-only causal LMs studied; no MLM or seq2seq variants.
Prompts not tuned per model, which may bias comparisons.
Social value tasks cover only six languages, five of them Romance; results inconclusive.
Models are 564M to 7.5B; larger scales not tested. Hypothesis that code-switching and shared sub-tokens explain cross-lingual prompting is not verified.
